# Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta (MN 139 (PTS MN iii 230))

**ID:** MN 139 (PTS MN iii 230)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Analysis of No Strife
**PTS:** MN iii 230
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

A full parallel is preserved in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 169, *Kurūsvaraṇā Sūtra*) and among Sanskrit manuscript fragments (SHT sutta13) [Huifeng 2012]. Unlike MN 139, MĀ 169 contains material praising the elder Subhūti as the foremost dweller in non-conflict (*araṇavihārin*) and explicitly links *araṇā* to emptiness (*śūnyatā*) [Huifeng 2012]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus aligns MN 139 strongly with MĀ 169 (T 26, fascicle 43) as well as the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, the *Mahāvastu*, and the *Lalitavistara* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records extensive shared phrasing with the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 4, AN 6, AN 8, AN 9, AN 10), and related Vibhaṅga discourses such as MN 137 and MN 140 [DharmaNexus].
